findings: The limiter buckets by `req.ip` (`const key = req.ip`) instead of by API key as documented ("Each API key is limited to 100 requests per minute"). In a shared-office scenario, many distinct API keys/users sit behind one NATed public IP, so they all share a single counter and collectively exhaust the 100-request bucket far faster than any single key should — exactly the reported symptom.

The counter has no time window at all: `buckets` is a plain Map that is incremented forever and never reset or expired based on elapsed time (no timestamp is stored, no per-minute rollover, no TTL/cleanup). This means the real behavior is a lifetime cap of 100 requests per key/IP, not '100 requests per minute' as documented — once tripped, the caller stays limited indefinitely rather than recovering after 60 seconds, compounding the shared-IP problem.

`checkLimit` returns only `{ limited: boolean }` with no timestamp or reset time recorded anywhere in the bucket, so there is no data available to compute the documented `Retry-After` header value. Since no window start/expiry is ever tracked, it is structurally impossible for any caller of this function to produce a correct `Retry-After`, contradicting the documented contract that a 429 response includes one.

The `buckets` Map grows unbounded, with an entry created and never evicted for every distinct `req.ip` seen — a memory leak / resource-exhaustion risk under high-cardinality traffic (e.g. many transient client IPs), independent of the rate-limit correctness issues above.
